title: Cyclone Koji crosses north Queensland coast
detail: Tropical Cyclone Koji crossed between Ayr and Bowen; BOM recorded 362mm at Clarke Range in 24h and 370mm at Cattle Creek in 12h, with severe weather warnings Proserpine to Gladstone; about 22,000 homes lost power.
attribution: BOM, QFES and Ergon Energy via ABC

title: Ex-Cyclone Koji flood emergency at Clermont
detail: Isaac Regional Council issued a flood emergency warning for Clermont; major flood warnings for the Georgina, Connors-Isaac and Flinders rivers, with swift-water rescues in Clermont, Gracemere and Mackay.
agency: Isaac Regional Council / Bureau of Meteorology
attribution: Isaac Regional Council, QSES and BOM via ABC

title: Victorian bushfires destroy 228 homes
detail: Fires that began 7 Jan burnt about 404,000 ha, destroyed 228 homes (Longwood fire 142, Ravenswood South 54, Walwa 9) and more than 700 structures; one farmer died in the Longwood fire, per CFA and state authorities.
attribution: CFA and State Control Centre via ABC

title: NSW Health measles alert for western Sydney
detail: NSW Health warned of exposure sites in St Clair and Nepean Hospital's emergency department after a confirmed measles case acquired in Thailand.
attribution: Alert issued by NSW Health

title: Illicit tobacco factory raided in Rouse Hill
detail: The Illicit Tobacco Taskforce with ATO, TGA and NSW Police raided a Rouse Hill self-storage unit, seizing a cigarette machine the ATO said could make up to 3.6 million cigarettes a day, 7.5 kg of loose tobacco, about 6,000 vape components and counterfeit packaging.
attribution: ABF/ATO media release

title: WA reports four meningococcal B cases since December
detail: WA Health reported four unlinked serogroup B meningococcal cases (two in December 2025, two in January 2026) and said this did not yet indicate an increase; WA had 13 cases and one death in 2025.
attribution: Figures as reported by WA Health

title: Daly River town evacuated ahead of flood peak
detail: NT authorities declared an emergency evacuation of about 450 Daly River residents to Darwin as a tropical low dumped 300-500mm on the catchment; water and sewerage expected to be cut once the river passed 14 m.
agency: NT Police, Fire and Emergency Services
attribution: NT emergency authorities and BOM via AAP

title: Perth Invasion Day rally bomb declared terrorist act
detail: WA Police declared the attempted bombing of the Invasion Day rally in Perth's CBD a terrorist act and a 31-year-old man was charged with engaging in a terrorist act, WA's first such charge; police said the homemade fragment bomb with ball bearings and screws was racially motivated and failed to cause casualties.
attribution: WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch via ABC

title: CACT obtains orders over nearly AUD 2m linked to drug syndicate
detail: The AFP said the Criminal Assets Confiscation Taskforce obtained a forfeiture order over AUD 1.7 million cash and restraining orders over about AUD 235,000 in other assets, including a boat, linked to alleged drug trafficking across Qld, NSW and the NT.
attribution: Claims by the AFP

title: OSB: three people-smuggling ventures resolved in February
detail: ABF's Operation Sovereign Borders update said three maritime people-smuggling ventures were resolved in February 2026 and 11 people returned to their country of departure (9 to country of origin); fewer than five were transferred to regional processing.
attribution: ABF/Joint Agency Task Force OSB monthly update

title: 1,336 road deaths in 12 months to February 2026
detail: BITRE reported 1,336 road deaths in the 12 months to February 2026, 4.4% higher than a year earlier, and 103 deaths in February 2026; calendar 2025 had 1,317 deaths.
attribution: Statistics published by BITRE

title: Chinese navy helicopter makes unsafe pass at RAN Seahawk
detail: Defence said a PLA-Navy helicopter closed to an unsafe distance and rolled toward an MH-60R from HMAS Toowoomba over the Yellow Sea during Operation Argos (UN sanctions monitoring on North Korea), forcing evasive action; no damage or injuries.
attribution: Australian Defence statement via USNI News

title: Victoria urges MMR vaccination as local measles spread
detail: Victoria's Department of Health reported 17 measles cases so far in 2026, including spread among people who had not travelled or visited known exposure sites.
attribution: Figures as reported by the Victorian Department of Health

title: Katherine River hits 20-year high
detail: Katherine River peaked at 19.2 m at Katherine Bridge, highest in more than 20 years; about 500 people sheltered in evacuation centres, 208 evacuated from Daly River and all of Palumpa evacuated, per NT SES and NT government.
attribution: NTSES, BOM and NT Chief Minister via CityNews

title: Covert operation leads to 26 men charged with 1,000+ child abuse offences
detail: AFP said a Victoria JACET covert operation into encrypted sharing of violent child abuse material led to 26 men charged with more than 1,000 offences, plus 9 arrested by NSW Police on referral; about 65,000 unique files identified.
attribution: AFP media release

title: Three killed in head-on crash on Kings Highway at Monga
detail: Police said a sedan crossed onto the wrong side of the Kings Highway at Monga, about 42km north-west of Batemans Bay, and hit a hatchback; three people died and four were hospitalised.
attribution: ABC News citing NSW Police

title: Cyclone Narelle upgraded to category 3
detail: BOM said Narelle was 780 km ENE of Cooktown with 165 km/h winds and could reach category 4 with gusts to 250 km/h before landfall between Lockhart River and Port Douglas; up to 450mm rain forecast.
attribution: BOM forecast via ABC

title: Narelle makes landfall in three states
detail: BOM said Narelle hit Queensland as a category 4 (20 Mar), the NT as a category 3 (22 Mar) and WA's North West Cape as a severe category 4 (27 Mar), travelling about 6,500 km; only the second system on record to hit all three states as a severe cyclone.
place: Cape York Peninsula / Top End / North West Cape
attribution: BOM post-event summary

title: Australians lost AUD 2.18bn to scams in 2025, NASC says
detail: The ACCC's National Anti-Scam Centre reported AUD 2.18 billion lost to scams in 2025, up 7.8% on 2024, from 481,523 combined reports; investment scams accounted for AUD 837.7 million.
attribution: Figures as reported by the ACCC/National Anti-Scam Centre (Targeting Scams report)

title: Two Moree teens charged over extremist material
detail: NSW JCTT charged a 15- and a 16-year-old from Moree with violent extremist material offences; police alleged they seized handwritten extremist notes and a ballistic-style vest.
attribution: AFP media release

title: Nine charged over multi-tonne cocaine import conspiracy
detail: AFP said nine men aged 31-72 across Victoria, Sydney and Perth were charged in Operation Bruce Cremorne, a 10-month probe begun after a trawler sank off Port Albert, over alleged conspiracies to import tonnes of cocaine.
attribution: AFP media release (with Victoria Police, ABF, ACIC)

title: ASIC removed nearly 12,000 scam websites in 2025
detail: ASIC said it removed 11,964 phishing and investment scam websites in calendar 2025, a 90% rise on the prior year, and warned AI is being used to power fake trading-bot and celebrity-endorsement investment scams.
attribution: Claims by ASIC (media release 26-063MR)

title: Cyclone Maila heads for Cape York
detail: BOM said Maila had weakened to category 2 and was expected to cross near Coen and Lockhart River the following week with gusts to 155 km/h; Queensland Health flagged melioidosis risk from heavy rain.
attribution: BOM via ABC

title: ABF apprehends two illegal fishing boats off Cape Wessel
detail: ABF officers from HMAS Cape Woolamai boarded and apprehended two foreign fishing vessels north of Cape Wessel, NT, finding evidence of fisheries offences; crews taken to Darwin.
attribution: ABF via Baird Maritime

title: Illegal fishing vessel seized in Torres Strait
detail: ABF patrol boat Storm Bay intercepted a suspected foreign fishing vessel near Mount Adolphus Island under Operation Broadstaff; ABF said it had intercepted 22 illegal foreign fishing vessels and seized over 6 tonnes of sea cucumber since 1 Jan 2026.
attribution: ABF via Baird Maritime

title: WA JOCTF: ten charged, AUD 1.13m cash and 114kg meth seized
detail: The AFP said a WA Joint Organised Crime Task Force investigation charged ten men and seized AUD 1,132,000 in suspected proceeds of crime plus 114kg methylamphetamine, 6.3kg heroin and 4kg ketamine; one South Australian man was charged with money laundering.
attribution: Allegations by the AFP; charges not yet tested in court

title: Canberra teen charged with planning terrorist act
detail: ACT Policing said a 17-year-old in custody since Nov 2025 was additionally charged with acts in preparation for a terrorist act, allegedly motivated by nationalist and racist views - the first such charge in the ACT.
attribution: ACT Policing media release

title: Three charged over BEC scam proceeds used to buy gold bullion
detail: AFP-led cybercrime detectives charged three people in Sydney over an alleged AUD 600,000 business email compromise scam, alleging about AUD 100,000 was converted into gold bullion; AUD 34,000 cash was seized and about AUD 300,000 recovered.
attribution: Allegations by the AFP; charges not yet tested in court

title: AFP: 17 tonnes of drugs seized in Pacific in 2026
detail: AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett told a Pacific Transnational Crime Summit in Suva that 17 t of illicit drugs, mostly cocaine, had been seized in early 2026 versus 4.6 t in all of 2025, calling Pacific trafficking a national security threat.
attribution: AFP Commissioner via PINA

title: Darwin teen charged over nationalist extremist material
detail: AFP charged a 16-year-old in Darwin with possessing and distributing violent extremist material promoting nationalist ideology and possessing a prohibited weapon.
attribution: AFP media release

title: NASC: 5,834 scam websites taken down in Q1 2026
detail: The National Anti-Scam Centre said 5,834 scam websites (including 1,960 fake gambling sites) were taken down in January-March 2026; Scamwatch received 45,816 reports with AUD 76.7 million lost, and combined Scamwatch/ReportCyber losses were AUD 248.3 million.
attribution: Figures as reported by the National Anti-Scam Centre

title: Cambodian scam compound scripted AFP impersonation calls to Australians
detail: The AFP said a compound at O'Smach, Cambodia, found by the Royal Thai Military in January 2026, ran scripted calls impersonating AFP officers; about 300 potential Australian victims were identified. The AFP said its Operation Firestorm has contributed to 560 arrests and disruption of 15 scam centres in the region.
attribution: Claims by the AFP

title: Clandestine drug lab found, six charged over AUD 39m cocaine
detail: AFP and ABF executed warrants at Kingsdale near Goulburn and in Sydney after 120 kg of cocaine was found in vehicle transmissions shipped from California; 44 kg cocaine and 2 kg meth found at an alleged lab. Six NSW men charged.
attribution: AFP media release

title: Record 2.7-tonne cocaine seizure (Operation Minjiang)
detail: AFP said 2.7 t of cocaine landed near Midge Point, Qld, was seized at a Londonderry property in western Sydney, bringing the operation to more than 3 t (street value about AUD 816 million); eight people charged.
attribution: AFP media release (with QPS, ABF, ACIC, AUSTRAC)

title: ASIO 2026 threat assessment keeps level at PROBABLE
detail: ASIO Director-General Mike Burgess kept the terrorism threat level at PROBABLE, warning of self-radicalising youths with blended nationalist, racist and anti-authority ideologies and alleging IRGC-linked actors were behind antisemitic attacks in Australia.
attribution: ASIO Director-General via Australian Security Magazine

title: Tranche 2 AML/CTF obligations take effect for professions
detail: AML/CTF obligations began applying on 1 July 2026 to lawyers, accountants, conveyancers, real estate professionals and precious-metal dealers; AUSTRAC opened enrolment on 31 March with a 29 July deadline, and an estimated 80,000-90,000 new reporting entities are expected.
attribution: Compliance-industry summary of AUSTRAC dates; entity estimate as stated by Legl

title: Killara man charged with laundering AUD 2.4m through construction firm
detail: The AFP charged a 45-year-old man from Sydney's North Shore with dealing in proceeds of crime, alleging he laundered AUD 2.4 million in syndicate cash through a construction business using false invoices between June 2024 and November 2025.
attribution: Allegations by the AFP; charge not yet tested in court

title: Nationwide Telstra outage disrupts 000 calls, trains and payments
detail: A Telstra outage from about 04:30 to 16:00 hit mobile and internet services in all states, disrupting some calls to the 000 emergency line, V/Line and NSW regional trains, the ARTC network and EFTPOS; Telstra blamed a time-synchronisation software defect and the minister said ACMA would investigate.
attribution: SBS News; cause as stated by Telstra

title: Secondary Telstra fault hits 000 calling
detail: Following the 8 July outage, a secondary fault caused error messages on calls to the 000 emergency line; Telstra said it had cut occurrences by about 90% overnight, and the report said over 100,000 customers were potentially affected.
attribution: WhistleOut report citing Telstra statements

title: Seized Myanmar scam compound shows romance scams aimed at Australians
detail: ABC reported that the Shunda Park compound in Myanmar's Karen State, taken by the KNLA and holding about 3,000 workers, ran romance and investment scams; a freed worker said older Australian women were targeted. The UN estimates at least 120,000 people are trapped in Myanmar compounds.
attribution: ABC News report; figures attributed to the UN and researchers cited in the article

title: Man fined AUD 31,000 over botched reptile smuggling
detail: A NSW man was fined AUD 31,000 for exporting fauna without authority after 65 reptiles taken near Narembeen and Merredin were posted from WA; parcels were intercepted at Perth and 55 of the animals died or were euthanised.
agency: WA Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions
attribution: DBCA case via ABC

title: ACMA sues Optus in Federal Court over 2025 Triple Zero outage
detail: ACMA began Federal Court action alleging Optus Mobile breached emergency-call rules on 1,005 occasions during the 18 September 2025 outage; the maximum penalty is AUD 250,000 per contravention.
attribution: Allegations by ACMA; not yet determined by the court

title: H5N1 bird flu detected in tern at Portland, Victoria
detail: Agriculture Victoria said preliminary testing found high pathogenicity H5N1 avian influenza in a greater crested tern at Portland, following detections in seabirds in WA, SA, NSW and Queensland; the emergency animal disease response plan was activated and human risk was described as very low.
attribution: Claims by Agriculture Victoria (preliminary test result)

title: Five die in fiery head-on crash on Stuart Highway
detail: NT Police said a ute travelling at excessive speed crossed into the path of a van about 2km south of the Marrakai Road turn-off south-east of Darwin; both vehicles caught fire and all five occupants died.
attribution: ABC News citing NT Police

title: AUSTRAC suspends Cryptolink, taking 96 crypto ATMs offline
detail: AUSTRAC suspended crypto ATM operator Cryptolink for three months, taking 96 machines offline, citing failures to lodge threshold transaction reports and weak ML/TF risk assessment; the firm had paid an AUD 56,340 infringement notice in 2025.
attribution: Crowdfund Insider report of AUSTRAC action; reasons as stated by AUSTRAC

title: Overhead wires fall on train, disrupting Sydney rail network
detail: Overhead wires came down on a South Coast Line train between Redfern and Erskineville around 16:30, isolating power on several tracks; hundreds of passengers were removed from three trains and services across Sydney were disrupted into the night.
attribution: ABC News citing Sydney Trains

title: 60 arrested in China-Australia tobacco smuggling takedown
detail: ABF and China Customs' Anti-Smuggling Bureau said Project Seahorse / Operation Trailblazer led to more than 60 arrests in China and seizure of over 60 million cigarettes in 91 containers bound for Sydney and other ports, with AUD 92 million in duty evaded.
attribution: ABF media release

title: Telcos issue new 000 calling advice after outages
detail: The Australian Telecommunications Alliance launched advice for calling the 000 emergency line during outages: hang up and redial if not connected within five seconds, then stay on the line up to a minute so the phone can find another network.
attribution: Advice issued by the Australian Telecommunications Alliance, as reported by EFTM

title: Bondi antisemitism royal commission ends hearings
detail: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion, set up after the 14 Dec 2025 Bondi Hanukkah attack that killed 15, closed hearings after 346 witnesses and over 20,000 submissions; final report due 18 Dec 2026.
agency: Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion
attribution: Royal commission via ABC

title: Two new Evolved Cape patrol boats commissioned in Cairns
detail: Navy commissioned HMAS Cape Spencer and HMAS Cape Hawke at HMAS Cairns for border protection and maritime constabulary work, with range over 4,000 nm.
attribution: Defence media release

title: Review finds Telstra failed to prioritise timing system behind July outage
detail: An independent review found the 8 July outage stemmed from a software update not applied to a GPS timing card; more than 600 calls to the 000 emergency line were unsuccessful. An ACMA investigation is ongoing, with fines of up to AUD 30 million possible.
attribution: SBS News; findings of the Telstra-commissioned independent review

title: Strike Force Myddleton: 33 charged over alleged AUD 600m loan fraud
detail: NSW Police allege a syndicate used false loan documents and inflated property deals to obtain up to AUD 600 million in loans, about AUD 500 million from the big four banks; 33 people have been charged and AUD 95 million in assets recovered, with the NSW Crime Commission, ATO and AUSTRAC involved.
attribution: Allegations by NSW Police as reported by ABC News

title: Optus outage blocks dozens of 000 calls in four jurisdictions
detail: An Optus network issue on a Friday caused intermittent call dropouts in Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the Northern Territory; about 39 calls to the 000 emergency line had connection difficulties, plus 3 in Tasmania.
place: Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania, Northern Territory
attribution: NewsBeep report citing Optus

title: Late flu peaks recorded in several states
detail: ABC reported late-season influenza rises: Queensland recorded about 3,435 cases in one week and Victoria a 400% rise over seven weeks, though national notifications remain well below 2025, when over 1,700 influenza-related deaths were recorded.
attribution: ABC News citing the Australian CDC and state health departments

title: Mildura-area outage leaves 2,700 customers without power for days
detail: A ute hit a critical power pole at Birdwoodton, cutting power to more than 2,700 homes and businesses from about 06:30 on 21 September; Powercor pushed restoration back to Friday.
attribution: ABC News; figures from Powercor

title: Security and ground-staff strikes hit Sydney and other airports
detail: About 400 Certis security staff at Sydney Airport held two-hour stoppages and TWU ground-service workers at Qantas subsidiaries began a 24-hour strike across Sydney, Adelaide, Brisbane and Perth; Qantas said it had contingency plans.
attribution: ABC News citing the TWU, Sydney Airport and Qantas

title: Bus with 18 aboard crashes on Melba Highway near Glenburn
detail: A public-transport bus carrying 17 passengers and a driver collided with two cars on the Melba Highway near Glenburn; a car driver died and six people were injured, two seriously.
attribution: ABC News citing Victoria Police and Ambulance Victoria
